label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: Every view (front, side, top, below and the four angles) shows a plain rectangular box with flat square corners. A 55-gallon drum is a cylinder with rounded sides and raised rims at top and bottom, so the outline is wrong in all six views.

M2.reason: Measured 23 x 23 x 34 units against a requested 23 across and 34 high, an offset of 0. The brief gives no drum size of its own, so the measured size is the one the harness asked for.

M3.reason: The drum's parts are missing: no rolling hoops or chimes at top and bottom, no bung, and no rounded body. The model is one solid block with no components beyond its six faces.

M4.reason: The whole block is a flat grey, mottled like concrete. The brief asks for rusted steel with yellow hazard paint, so the colour and material are clearly off on the only region there is.

M5.reason: No hazard stripe anywhere on any face, and no rust or wear beyond a faint mottling that could be grain. The brief's two named markings, the hazard stripe and the rust, are both absent.

M6.reason: In the line-up (B) it reads as a grey box beside a rock, a bone, and a checkered ball. No player would take it for a drum, and it has the look of the plain-box decoy the rubric says must fail.

M7.reason: It stands upright on its origin, which suits a drum. But with no stripe, rim or other marking, nothing shows a front, so the facing cannot be confirmed against what the brief asks for.

M8.reason: The harness reports no check errors. It has 12 triangles, far under twice the Half-Life median of 62 and under the third quartile of 156. The box is closed, with nothing open, inside out or floating.
